_comment: Traces a reader should be able to follow. Each is a *directed* search: the
point of a trace is that a request, or an explanation, flows one way, and a
route that only exists backwards is not the answer to the question.
`viaRelationships` constrains what the route may be made of but not its
length, because more than one correct route often exists at different
altitudes — method-to-method and class-to-class — and pinning one of them
would be pinning an implementation detail of the search rather than a fact

paths.name: Contract to storage: a documented operation reaches the table it writes
Route to storage: the served route reaches the same table
Specification to schema: a promised operation reaches a column
Prose to data: the README reaches the table its subject writes
Deployment to database: compose reaches the provider it runs
Migration to column: the schema file reaches what it declared
Prose to handler: the README reaches the method that serves users
paths.note: README -> #users -> UserController -> create. Deliberately not the other direction: ROUTES_TO runs from the route into the code, so no route reaches an api node from a document, and asserting one would be asserting an edge that should not exist.
